title: Bahadur Shah's Audience Bolsters Gulab Rai's Rival Seat

blocks.text: This page frames episode 76 around imperial recognition: Bahadur Shah visited Sirhind, asked whether any descendant of Guru Gobind Singh remained, and Sulakhan Masand presented Gulab Rai as the claimant fit for an audience.

The meeting is narrated with borrowed reverence, as Sulakhan Masand arranged a meeting between the emperor and Gulab Rai and the court addressed him as Ramdas while treating the encounter in the same ceremonial manner once shown to the Sikh Gurus.
That borrowed prestige matters because Gulab Rai then set up his own pontifical seat, turning court favour and inherited symbolism into a rival center of authority.
